acceptedAnswer.text: It is the sales volume at which total revenue equals total costs, so profit is exactly zero. Above it you make a profit and below it you make a loss.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between margin and markup?

acceptedAnswer.text: Margin is profit divided by the selling price, and markup is profit divided by the cost. A product costing $100 sold at $150 has a 33.3% margin but a 50% markup.
It is the selling price minus the variable cost of a unit. It is the amount each sale contributes toward covering fixed costs and then profit.

mainEntity.name: What is the margin of safety?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is how far sales can fall before you hit break-even, shown here as a percentage of your target volume. A bigger cushion means lower risk.

mainEntity.name: How do I lower my break-even point?

acceptedAnswer.text: Raise the price, reduce variable costs per unit, or cut fixed costs. The sensitivity table shows how much a 5% or 10% change in price or variable cost moves the number of units.
